findings.title: Unsandboxed Windows commands can access outside-workspace resources without user approval
findings.evidence: Windows invokes host process/spawn without a Codex filesystem/network sandbox. Risk strategy version 0 skips approval for every COMMAND. Version 1 auto-approves commands such as mvn test and python -m unittest, which execute workspace-controlled build/test code.
findings.impact: A command can read or modify files outside the workspace or access the network without explicit user authorization, contrary to the confirmed boundary.
findings.requested_change: Require explicit approval for unsandboxed Windows command execution, or restrict auto-approved commands to a set that cannot execute workspace-controlled code or access outside resources; ensure risk strategy version 0 cannot bypass this boundary.

findings.title: Capability preflight validates command/exec but not process/spawn
findings.evidence: The Windows adapter calls process/spawn, while the generated-schema preflight requires only CommandExecParams fields. A server without process/spawn can still advertise guarded-command-v1 and only fail when a command is invoked.
findings.impact: Worker readiness can report a Windows command capability that the installed App Server cannot execute.
findings.requested_change: Probe the process/spawn method and the request fields used by Windows before advertising guarded-command-v1.

findings.title: Missing App Server diagnostic still describes sandbox isolation as the dependency
findings.evidence: CODEX_EXECUTABLE_UNAVAILABLE maps to wording that says Windows command isolation requires Codex App Server, although the new path uses it only to execute commands without a Codex sandbox.
findings.impact: The diagnostic suggests an obsolete isolation requirement and can send users to the wrong setup path.
findings.requested_change: Change the message to state that Windows command execution requires an installed Codex App Server.

acceptance.criteria: Windows command uses the configured executable, workspace cwd, and bounded environment payload.
acceptance.result: supported statically, with an authorization finding
acceptance.evidence: argv is taken from the fixed command policy with Python/PowerShell executable normalization; cwd uses safe_path; process/spawn receives the configured command, resolved cwd, and explicit environment map. The API child environment remains unsandboxed.

acceptance.criteria: Commands that may access outside the workspace require explicit authorization.
acceptance.evidence: Windows process/spawn is unsandboxed; version 0 auto-allows all commands and version 1 auto-allows build/test commands that execute workspace-controlled code.

acceptance.criteria: Timeout, output limit, cancellation, and Job Object cleanup are retained.
acceptance.evidence: Request includes timeoutMs/outputBytesCap, output events are accumulated and checked against the configured cap, cancellation interrupts event receive, and finally closes the Job after TerminateJobObject/ActiveProcesses confirmation. Actual App Server behavior was not run.

acceptance.criteria: Installed App Server support is diagnosed before Windows command capability is advertised.
acceptance.evidence: Preflight only requires CommandExecParams, not process/spawn.

acceptance.criteria: Missing App Server has an actionable message that matches its role.
acceptance.evidence: AIW_CODEX_PATH and external Worker are named, but the message still calls this a command-isolation dependency.

acceptance.criteria: Linux/WSL retains cgroup-limited sandboxed command/exec behavior.
acceptance.evidence: The Linux branch retains generated sandbox config, command/exec, cgroup resource limits, kill and populated=0 confirmation; the changed Windows path is selected when no Linux cgroup group exists.
